variables-and-types.prompt: Which of the following is a value type in C# allocated on the stack (when local)?
options: A) System.String
B) System.Int32
C) System.Object
D) System.Array
variables-and-types.explanation: In C#, structs such as `System.Int32` (int) are value types, holding their data directly rather than an object reference on the managed heap.
variables-and-types.hint: Primitive numeric types in C# are defined as structs.

variables-and-types.prompt: What does the following C# code print to the console?
variables-and-types.code_snippet:
int? val = null;
Console.WriteLine(val.GetValueOrDefault(42));
options: A) null
D) Throws InvalidOperationException
variables-and-types.explanation: `GetValueOrDefault(default)` returns the assigned value if `HasValue` is true, or the supplied fallback parameter if null.
variables-and-types.hint: Check what happens when val has no value.

variables-and-types.prompt: Which keyword enables local variable type inference in C# where the compiler determines the type at compile-time?
variables-and-types.code_snippet: var count = 100;
options: A) dynamic
B) object
C) var
D) auto
variables-and-types.explanation: `var` provides compile-time implicit typing. The variable remains strongly-typed as `int`.
variables-and-types.hint: It is three letters and statically typed, unlike dynamic.

variables-and-types.prompt: What is the result of casting a double with decimal points to an int in C#?
options: D) Compilation Error
variables-and-types.explanation: Explicit casting from floating-point types (`double`, `float`) to integer types truncates the fractional portion towards zero, resulting in 9.
variables-and-types.hint: Explicit numeric casting truncates rather than rounds.

variables-and-types.prompt: Which struct represents arbitrary contiguous regions of memory (stack, heap, or unmanaged) without allocating memory?
options: A) ArraySegment<T>
B) Span<T>
C) List<T>
D) MemoryStream
variables-and-types.explanation: `Span<T>` is a stack-only `ref struct` that provides a type-safe and memory-safe representation of contiguous memory.
variables-and-types.hint: Introduced in C# 7.2 / .NET Core 2.1 for high-performance zero-allocation operations.
